title: Inspiring teens
grammar: Past simple and present perfect for telling life stories, plus gerunds and infinitives

vocab.example: She is an inspiring young activist.
vocab.example2: She has become one of the most inspiring voices of her generation.

vocab.example: The teenage entrepreneur started her own company.
vocab.example2: He has already launched two companies, and he is only nineteen.

vocab.example: Winning the prize was a huge achievement.
vocab.example2: Her greatest achievement was starting the project on her own.

vocab.example: Athletes can be role models for young people.
vocab.example2: He has been a role model for his younger brother since 2019.

vocab.example: Together, we are stronger — that is solidarity.
vocab.example2: The town showed real solidarity after the floods.

vocab.example: Her project had a real impact on the community.
vocab.example2: Have you ever had an impact on someone else's life?

vocab.example: He overcame a lot of difficulties before succeeding.
vocab.example2: She has overcome far more obstacles than most people realise.

vocab.example: Her determination is what makes the story worth telling.
vocab.example2: It was determination, not luck, that got her there.

student.repte: We often hear about inspiring teenage entrepreneurs and their successful stories but, who of you will be able to find the most amazing?

products.desc: In small groups, research an inspiring young person and share their story and impact as a video, podcast, digital poster or speech.
Present to the class and take questions from your classmates about the person your group chose.

teacher.repte: The opening Learning Scenario of the year, following the introductory session and the diagnostic test. Students discover the accomplishments of inspiring teens and young adults, and see how much more people achieve with a sense of solidarity — the “Together, we are stronger!” slogan.
teacher.competencies: Llengua Estrangera 2, 7 and 8; Ciutadana CC1; Emprenedora CE1; CPSAA 3; Digital CD2.
teacher.methodology: Project-Based Learning, collaborative learning with peer review, digital literacy for multimodal presentations, student-centred choice of topic.
teacher.assessment: Interpretation of oral and multimodal texts, audience engagement and creativity of the presentation, reliability of the sources used.

title: Art through words
grammar: Comparatives and superlatives for describing an artist's style and work

vocab.example: Her artwork is displayed in a small gallery.
vocab.example2: This artwork is far more colourful than the one beside it.

vocab.example: His later style is bolder than his early work.
vocab.example2: Her early style was simpler than the work she makes today.

vocab.example: The sculptor works mainly in bronze.
vocab.example2: He is the most original sculptor in the exhibition.

vocab.example: Creativity is at the heart of this project.
vocab.example2: Her creativity is greater than her technical skill, and that is the point.

vocab.example: The exhibition opens next week.
vocab.example2: This exhibition is smaller but much better organised than last year's.

vocab.example: Persistence helped her become a professional artist.
vocab.example2: Persistence matters more than talent in the long run.

vocab.example: The brushstrokes are looser than in the earlier painting.
vocab.example2: You can see the brushstrokes far more clearly in the original.

vocab.example: This portrait is the most striking piece in the room.
vocab.example2: It is the most famous portrait she ever painted.

student.repte: Art is not just old paintings in a museum. Find an artist who deserves to be better known — research their life and their work, and present them to the class as a team.

products.desc: Choose two comparable pieces and write ten comparative sentences describing the differences between them.
Present an unknown professional artist — sculptor, painter or photographer — covering their style and specific works. Use comparatives throughout. Slides carry keywords only, never full text.
A written listicle covering several aspects of the artist, following the structure of the model provided.

teacher.repte: Students find out about people who applied their creativity and initiative to produce art of various kinds, discovering that art is a living, vibrant form of expression. The group work develops suggesting ideas, listening respectfully, dividing tasks equally and giving constructive feedback.
teacher.competencies: Llengua Estrangera 3, 5 and 6; Ciutadana CC1; Emprenedora CE3; CPSAA 4; Digital CD3.
teacher.methodology: Project-Based Learning in mixed-ability groups, online research, peer review, digital creation tools. The comparison task is the grammar scaffold for the presentation.
teacher.assessment: Accurate and varied use of comparatives, quality of research and selection of information, ability to speak from keywords rather than read from the slide.

title: Saving Planet Earth
grammar: Present continuous for current trends, zero and first conditionals, and connectors

vocab.example: Air pollution is a serious problem in big cities.
vocab.example2: Pollution is getting worse in the city centre, although the council denies it.

vocab.example: Climate change affects the whole planet.
vocab.example2: If we ignore climate change, the problem will only grow.

vocab.example: We produce too much plastic waste.
vocab.example2: We are producing more waste than ever before.

vocab.example: Recycling helps reduce landfill.
vocab.example2: If you recycle glass, it can be reused almost indefinitely.

vocab.example: Sustainability means thinking about the future.
vocab.example2: The school is taking sustainability seriously this year.

vocab.example: Greenhouse gases trap heat in the atmosphere.
vocab.example2: If greenhouse gases increase, temperatures rise.

vocab.example: Our school is organising a green campaign.
vocab.example2: We are launching the campaign next Monday, so we need the posters now.

vocab.example: The poster raises awareness about single-use plastic.
vocab.example2: If we raise awareness at school, families will hear about it too.

student.repte: What are the biggest threats facing our planet? Research them, then design a campaign that persuades your classmates to actually do something about it.

products.desc: Research the global and local threats facing Earth and present a persuasive campaign with interactive elements.
Track what you Know, Want to know and have Learned, and record the sources you used and why they are reliable.
Practise reading the campaign text aloud — clear pronunciation, pausing at the punctuation, looking up any word you cannot say.

teacher.repte: Students analyse global and local environmental problems, evaluate the reliability of their sources, and develop a creative environmental campaign proposal cooperatively.
teacher.competencies: Llengua Estrangera 1, 4 and 9; Ciutadana CC3; Emprenedora CE1; CPSAA 4; Digital CD2.
teacher.methodology: Project-Based Learning, mind-mapping and KWL charts, source-reliability work, cooperative campaign design, digital poster and video tools.
teacher.assessment: Reliability and variety of sources, persuasive use of conditionals and connectors, ability to separate main from secondary ideas.

title: A Sci-Fi High-Tech Trip
grammar: Future forms and the second conditional, plus the register of a polite client email

vocab.example: The Moon is an unusual holiday destination.
vocab.example2: By 2100, this destination will be fully booked.

vocab.example: The accommodation includes a low-gravity room.
vocab.example2: If I could choose, I would book the accommodation with the Earth view.

vocab.example: The launch is scheduled for next spring.
vocab.example2: The launch is going to take place at dawn.

vocab.example: The hotel is in orbit around the Moon.
vocab.example2: We will be travelling in orbit for two days before we land.

vocab.example: You need a spacesuit to walk outside.
vocab.example2: If you forgot your spacesuit, you would not last a minute outside.

vocab.example: Design your trip with an unlimited budget.
vocab.example2: If I had an unlimited budget, I would add a zero-gravity pool.

vocab.example: Day three of the itinerary is a crater walk.
vocab.example2: I am attaching the full itinerary for your consideration.

vocab.example: We received an enquiry from a client about the price.
vocab.example2: Could you tell me whether your enquiry concerns the March departure?

student.repte: You have an unlimited budget and the whole solar system to work with. Can you design a high-tech trip nobody could refuse — and answer your clients convincingly when they write to you?

products.desc: In teams, plan the trip — travel logistics, accommodation, activities and challenges — and produce a brochure, web page or promotional video.
Answer real enquiries from your 'clients' in a polite, correctly structured email. Practised first in the TOD translation and email workshops.
Deliver the advertisement to the class, including the interactive elements, and field questions afterwards.

teacher.repte: Halfway through the year, students take a look at the future. Combining future thinking with travel, they reflect on how leisure might change, weigh the ethical, social and environmental impacts of high-tech tourism, and learn to appreciate the world as it is now.
teacher.competencies: Llengua Estrangera 2, 5 and 10; Ciutadana CC1; Emprenedora CE3; CPSAA 2; Digital CD5.
teacher.methodology: Project-Based Learning, shared Padlet for vocabulary, KWL charts, source evaluation, differentiated output (brochure, website or video). Email register is scaffolded across three TOD workshops: translation, then games.
teacher.assessment: Persuasive use of future forms and the second conditional, appropriate register and structure in the client emails, quality of the multimedia product.

title: School days
grammar: Modals of obligation and prohibition, for-and-against connectors, and the second conditional

vocab.example: Our timetable changes every term.
vocab.example2: Students must follow the timetable, although there is some flexibility.

vocab.example: The school has excellent sports facilities.
vocab.example2: If we designed the school, the facilities would be open at weekends.

vocab.example: Students there have to wear a uniform.
vocab.example2: You don't have to wear a uniform here, however many schools require one.

vocab.example: School rules are not the same in every country.
vocab.example2: School rules should be decided with the students, not just for them.

vocab.example: Students should have responsibilities too.
vocab.example2: Older students have to take on more responsibilities.

vocab.example: We get a twenty-minute break in the morning.
vocab.example2: You mustn't leave the building during the break.

vocab.example: They aren't allowed to use phones in class.
vocab.example2: In my ideal school, students would be allowed to choose two subjects.

vocab.example: In some schools you get detention for being late.
vocab.example2: You shouldn't get detention for forgetting a pencil.

student.repte: If you could design your ideal school, what would it look like? What rules would you implement? Uniform or free expression? What would the students' responsibilities be — if any?

products.desc: A visual presentation or digital brochure advertising your school. No text allowed except the title — use images. You may not read from a script or the screen: you must speak naturally. Use must, have to and should, plus the for-and-against connectors from your essay.
Write a for-and-against essay about rules at school, following the structure of the model provided.
Act out a conversation about a personal anecdote at school, paying particular attention to pronunciation and accent.

teacher.repte: The academic world opens the last term. Students learn about the difficult journeys some children make to reach school, give their opinion on the controversial topic of school uniforms, and consider the purpose of school rules and collective decision-making.
teacher.competencies: Llengua Estrangera 3, 5 and 7; Ciutadana CC1; Emprenedora CE3; CPSAA 4; Digital CD1.
teacher.methodology: Project-Based Learning, group decision-making through presenting, suggesting, evaluating and voting, comparative study of education systems. The no-text/no-script rule forces genuine speaking rather than reading aloud.
teacher.assessment: Accuracy of modals of obligation and the second conditional, balance and structure of the for-and-against essay, ability to present without a script.

title: Thinking outside the box
grammar: The passive voice for describing inventions and the second conditional for hypotheses

vocab.example: The printing press was a life-changing invention.
vocab.example2: The telephone was invented long before anyone imagined the internet.

vocab.example: The inventor never gave up on her idea.
vocab.example2: The inventor was never paid for her design.

vocab.example: Resilience matters when your first design fails.
vocab.example2: If you had more resilience, you would keep trying after a failure.

vocab.example: They came up with an innovative solution.
vocab.example2: The most innovative ideas are often rejected at first.

vocab.example: Problem-solving is the heart of this project.
vocab.example2: Problem-solving is taught through projects rather than exercises.

vocab.example: We built a cardboard prototype first.
vocab.example2: The prototype was built from recycled parts.

vocab.example: Explain which materials your invention is made of.
vocab.example2: If the materials were cheaper, we would produce it at scale.

vocab.example: They came up with the idea in five minutes.
vocab.example2: If you came up with a better design, we would build it.

student.repte: If you had all the necessary resources, what contribution would you make to human evolution? Will you be innovative enough to create something that makes our life easier or better?

products.desc: In groups, choose a real problem — at school, in town or global — brainstorm solutions, then design an invention and present its design, materials and how it works.
Record how your group took turns, expressed agreement and disagreement, and assigned tasks to reach a joint decision.

teacher.repte: The last stop of the year. Students learn about life-changing inventions and the inventors whose creativity, persistence and resilience produced them, then experience the satisfaction of contributing to society with their own creativity. NOTE: this scenario has not yet been delivered in any recorded year — the course has consistently run out of time after unit 5.
teacher.competencies: Llengua Estrangera 2, 3 and 4; Ciutadana CC1; Emprenedora CE3; CPSAA 4; Digital CD1.
teacher.methodology: Collaborative project work, brainstorming and negotiation, conversational strategies for turn-taking and agreement, digital tools for shaping ideas.
teacher.assessment: Fluency and self-confidence while speaking, comprehension of written texts about the origins of an invention, quality of group negotiation.
